description:
PERF, cause NOT found (s540d, 2026-11-15): on the s540d tree a one-pair `bless` loop in a program where some class has a DESTROY reads ~7 % slower than main in bench-exec, while the same loop with no DESTROY anywhere is equal.

MEASURED (heavy.sh bench, quiet; bench-exec rows blessnew-d / blessdes = s538b's weak-registry cost rows; scratch/s540d/legs/bench2..4.log in the s540d worktree):
- K=5, tree vs 24988e35: blessnew -7.6, blessnew-d -11.6, blessdes -9.6 %.
- K=9, tree vs 24988e35 (band = base vs base): blessnew -10.0 (band +0.6), blessnew-d -12.0 (+2.2), blessdes -10.7 (+0.8).
- After the #4984 fix-forward (a hash constructor of up to 7 pairs uses SBCL's default make-hash-table again; a computed :size cost ~33 ns a hash), K=9, tree vs 75904a35: blessnew -1.5 (band -0.5) -- FIXED; blessnew-d -7.3 (band -0.2), blessdes -6.8 (band +0.2) -- a residue.
- In-process `time` of the blessnew-d program (rp/blessnewd.pl): the tree CONSES LESS (1.021 vs 1.053 GB a run, the p-hash no-copy), GC time the same (~0.03 s); whole runs of the SAME core vary 0.60 -> 0.95 s back to back (system time 0.15-0.22 s: the gigabyte of fresh pages), so the whole-run A/B cannot see a 7 % effect.

NOT the cause, by reading: the bless path itself (p-bless, the s538b registry) is unchanged by s540d; the emission of the program is identical (paths aside); the autoflush mirror is not reached (no $|).  Candidates to measure: sb-sprof of the two cores on blessnew-d (allocation profile: does the weak registry see a different object mix?), and the core's layout (s539d saw 5-10 % on two loop rows with byte-identical emission).

BAR: blessnew-d / blessdes inside the base-vs-base band on a quiet box, or the cause named.
subject: PERF, cause not found: on the s540d tree the DESTROY-registry bless rows (bench-exec blessnew-d / blessdes) read ~7 % slower than main (band <= 0.2 %); the plain bless row is equal after the #4984 fix-forward
